questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Suhana told her that she would be watching the birds.

options.text: Suhana said to her, "I will be watching the birds."
Suhana said to me, "I would be watching the birds."
Suhana told her, "she will be watching the birds."
Suhana said to her, "I must be watching the birds".

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Suhana said to her, "I will be watching the birds." .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **indirect speech**, where Suhana is reporting something to someone about her own action in the future.
 
• To convert this to **direct speech**, we need to use the exact words spoken by Suhana. Since she is referring to herself, the pronoun **"I"** must be used instead of "she."
 
• The future tense "would be watching" in indirect speech changes to "will be watching" in direct speech because the reporting verb "told" indicates a simple statement.

Correct sentence: *Suhana said to her, "I will be watching the birds."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for Direct and Indirect Speech:**
 
 
• In direct speech, the exact words of the speaker are placed within quotation marks.
 
• Pronouns and tenses may need to be adjusted when converting between direct and indirect speech depending on the context.
 
 
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• Indirect Speech: She said that she would come to the party.
 
• Direct Speech: She said, "I will come to the party."
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Fill in the blanks with the correct tense forms, maintaining consistency with future time reference and ongoing action. This time next year, she __________ (complete) her doctoral thesis and __________ (work) as a full-time lecturer at the university.

options.text: will have completed, will be working

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2' i.e. will have completed, will be working.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence refers to **future time reference** and involves two actions: one that will be completed and another that will be ongoing at a specific point in the future.
 
• The correct tense to describe an action that will be completed by a specific time in the future is the **future perfect tense** (will have + past participle).
 
• The correct tense to describe an action that will be ongoing at a specific point in the future is the **future continuous tense** (will be + present participle).

Correct sentence: *This time next year, she **will have completed** her doctoral thesis and **will be working** as a full-time lecturer at the university.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Future Perfect Tense:**

 
 
• **Structure:** will have + past participle.
 
• **Example:** By 2025, I will have graduated from college.
 
• **Usage:** Describes actions that will be completed before a specific time in the future.
 
 
 
• **Future Continuous Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure:** will be + present participle.
 
• **Example:** This time tomorrow, I will be flying to Paris.
 
• **Usage:** Describes actions that will be ongoing at a specific point in the future.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The wall was being climbed by the ivy which had been planted years ago.

options.text: The ivy, which had been planted years ago, was climbing the wall.
The ivy, which was planted years ago, is climbing the wall.
The ivy which someone planted years ago climbed the wall.
The ivy which had been planted years ago had climbed the wall.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. The ivy, which had been planted years ago, was climbing the wall .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **passive voice**: "The wall was being climbed by the ivy which had been planted years ago."
 
• To convert it into the **active voice**, the focus shifts from the object (the wall) to the subject (the ivy).
 
• The subject (the ivy) performs the action (climbing the wall).
 
• Option 1, **"The ivy, which had been planted years ago, was climbing the wall,"** correctly expresses the sentence in the active voice while maintaining the original meaning.

Correct sentence: *The ivy, which had been planted years ago, was climbing the wall*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active Voice:**
 
 
• The subject of the sentence performs the action.
 
• **Example:** The dog chased the ball.
 
 
 
• **Passive Voice:**
 
 
• The object of the sentence becomes the focus, and the subject is either omitted or introduced later.
 
• **Example:** The ball was chased by the dog.
 
 
 
• When converting from passive to active voice:
 
 
• Identify the subject, verb, and object in the passive sentence.
 
• Rearrange the sentence so that the subject performs the action.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the suitable word.

Neither the teacher nor the students _____ aware of the new rule.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**were**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When subjects are joined by "**neither...nor**", the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it.
 
• Here, the nearest subject is "**students**", which is plural.
 
• The sentence is also in the past context, so the correct plural past tense verb is "**were**".
 
• **Options 1, 2, and 4** do not agree correctly with the subject and tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

**Complete Sentence:** *"Neither the teacher nor the students **were**__ aware of the new rule."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "was"** is singular and does not agree with the plural noun "students".
 
• **Option 2: "is"** is singular present tense, which is incorrect here.
 
• **Option 4: "has"** is singular and does not agree with the plural noun "students".

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(1) Having been living in the secluded monastery for over twenty years, / (2) the monk possessed a perspective on the transience of material wealth / (3) that was fundamentally different from the visitors who traveled / (4) from the bustling cities to seek his spiritual guidance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Having been living .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in part **(1)**: "Having been living in the secluded monastery for over twenty years."
 
• The phrase **"Having been living"** is incorrect because it is unnecessarily complex and grammatically inappropriate in this context.
 
• The correct structure should be **"Having lived"**, which simplifies the sentence while maintaining proper grammar.
 
• The corrected sentence would read: "Having lived in the secluded monastery for over twenty years, the monk possessed a perspective on the transience of material wealth."

Correct sentence: *Having lived in the secluded monastery for over twenty years, the monk possessed a perspective on the transience of material wealth that was fundamentally different from the visitors who traveled from the bustling cities to seek his spiritual guidance.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The phrase **"Having been living"** is a combination of the perfect continuous tense in the passive form, which is rarely used and is not appropriate here. Instead, the use of **"Having lived"** (perfect participle) is simpler and grammatically correct.
 
• **Perfect participles** (like "Having lived") are often used to describe actions that were completed before another action.
 
• For example:
 
 
• **Incorrect:** Having been studying for hours, she took a break.
 
• **Correct:** Having studied for hours, she took a break.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
A sentence has been divided into four parts and jumbled. Out of the four alternatives suggested, choose the option showing correct sequence of the jumbled sentences and mark your answer.

P. The Pulitzer Prize for Criticism has been presented since 1970 for 'distinguished criticism'.
Q. there are friendly criticisms, amicably discussed and
R. Criticism is often presented as something unpleasant, but
S. some people find great pleasure in criticism.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. RQSP .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The question presents a jumbled sentence divided into four parts: P, Q, R, and S.
 
• To form a coherent sentence, the parts need to be arranged logically and grammatically.
 
• The correct sequence is **RQSP** because:
 
 
• Part R introduces the idea that criticism is often perceived as unpleasant.
 
• Part Q continues this thought by discussing "friendly criticisms."
 
• Part S adds a contrasting idea, stating that some people enjoy criticism.
 
• Part P concludes the sentence by introducing the Pulitzer Prize as a positive example of criticism.
 
 

Correct sentence: *Criticism is often presented as something unpleasant, but there are friendly criticisms, amicably discussed and some people find great pleasure in criticism. The Pulitzer Prize for Criticism has been presented since 1970 for 'distinguished criticism'.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When solving jumbled sentence questions:
 
 
• Look for logical connectors like "but," "and," and "however" to identify relationships between parts.
 
• Identify the main subject and supporting ideas to establish the correct sequence.
 
 
 
• Practice regularly to improve speed and accuracy in arranging sentences.
</ul

questions.question: I did not mind what he was saying as he was only __talking through his hat.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. talking nonsense .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The expression **"talking through his hat"** is an idiom, meaning to speak without knowledge or to talk nonsense.
 
• It is often used to describe a situation where a person is making statements that are illogical, inaccurate, or baseless.
 
• Among the given options, the most suitable meaning of the idiom is **"talking nonsense."**

Correct sentence: *I did not mind what he was saying as he was only **talking nonsense**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other idiomatic meanings:**

 
 
• **"Talking insultingly":** To speak in a disrespectful or offensive manner. This is not the correct meaning of the idiom in the given context.
 
• **"Talking irresponsibly":** To speak without considering the consequences. While this may seem related, it does not match the idiom's meaning here.
 
• **"Talking ignorantly":** To speak without proper knowledge. Although similar, this is not the best match for the idiom's intended meaning in this sentence.
 
 
 
• **Common usage:** The idiom "talking through his hat" is often used in informal contexts to dismiss someone's statements as baseless or nonsensical.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Imbroglio
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Agreement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Imbroglio"** refers to a complicated or confused situation, often involving conflict or misunderstanding. (उलझन या विवाद)

 
 
• **Example:** The diplomatic imbroglio between the two nations lasted for several months.
 
 
 
• **"Agreement"** is the opposite of imbroglio, as it signifies harmony, mutual understanding, or a consensus between parties. (समझौता या सहमति)
 
 
• **Example:** The two companies reached an agreement to collaborate on the new project.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the antonym of **"Imbroglio"** is **"Agreement"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Agreement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example:** The sudden complication in the surgery required immediate attention.

• **Example:** The land dispute between the neighbors escalated into a legal battle.

questions.question:
In the following question, there are six sentences marked S1, S6, P, Q, R, S. The positions of S1 and S6 are fixed. You are required to choose one of the four alternatives which would be the most logical sequence of the sentence in the passage. 
 S1. Widowhood in India used to be especially miserable. 
 P: There were widows even in ages ranging from five to ten. 
 Q: A widow was a widow always. 
 R: However, several communities began to rebel against the ill-treatments of widows. 
 S: She could not marry again however tender in age she might be. 
 S6. Today nobody looks upon remarriage of widows with disgust or disapproval.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. QSPR .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage discusses the miserable condition of widows in India in the past and progresses toward how societal attitudes have changed.
 
• The logical sequence should reflect the progression from the description of past conditions to the eventual reform and current situation.
 
• The correct sequence of sentences is **QSPR**:
 
 
• **Q:** A widow was a widow always (general statement about the condition).
 
• **S:** She could not marry again however tender in age she might be (specific detail).
 
• **P:** There were widows even in ages ranging from five to ten (further elaboration).
 
• **R:** However, several communities began to rebel against the ill-treatment of widows (transition to change).
 
 
 
• The final sentence, S6, concludes the passage by stating the current societal acceptance of widow remarriage.

Correct sequence: *QSPR*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **How to Approach Sentence Rearrangement Questions:**
 
 
• Identify the fixed sentences (S1 and S6 in this case) and understand their role in the passage.
 
• Look for logical connections between sentences (e.g., cause-effect, general-specific, transition words).
 
• Ensure the sequence maintains a coherent flow from the introduction to the conclusion.
 
 
 
• **Reason for Choosing QSPR:**
 
 
• Sentence Q introduces the general state of widows in the past, forming a strong opening for the logical sequence.
 
• Sentence S elaborates on the condition of widows, followed by the specific detail in P.
 
• Sentence R provides the transition to the reform and societal change, leading naturally to the concluding S6.
 
 
</ul

• The passage explains that digital literacy involves the ability to navigate digital platforms safely and effectively.
 
• It includes skills such as evaluating online sources critically, understanding cybersecurity practices, and recognizing the impact of digital footprints.
 
• Digital literacy also involves ethical behaviour, responsible sharing of information, and awareness of privacy and data rights.
 
• Therefore, digital literacy primarily refers to the **ability to use digital systems responsibly and critically**, rather than merely owning devices or having technical expertise.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: Owning smartphones** – Simply possessing a digital device does not ensure the knowledge or ability to use it safely and effectively.
 
• **Option 3: Coding expertise** – Coding is a specialized technical skill, whereas digital literacy is a broader concept that includes safe and responsible digital usage.
 
• **Option 4: Internet speed** – Internet speed relates to infrastructure or connectivity and is not a measure of a person’s ability to understand and use digital systems responsibly.
